parentSnapshots.body:
## Executive verdict

`agent-cli` still has no product-reachable MCP client path, but this issue is a **broad P0 parent initiative**, not one executable Task. Independent depth triage and proposal review established ten separate cause/security boundaries plus two existing issues to reuse. Do not implement this parent directly.

Revalidated against `origin/develop` `f14b164ba7ef402458f0cf08c69ff920dce9966c` and the current official documentation on 2026-08-29.

## Current observed state

- No deployable package under `packages/` or `apps/` consumes `@robota-sdk/agent-tool-mcp` or `@robota-sdk/agent-transport-mcp`; `scratch/package.json` is a non-product consumer and does not make the feature reachable.
- Production code under `packages/agent-cli/src` and `packages/agent-command/src` has no `mcpServers` setting, `/mcp` command, server-level client, catalog, or composition path.
- The framework plugin loader reads `.mcp.json` as `mcpConfig?: unknown`, but production code does not type, resolve, approve, or activate it.
- The private `agent-tool-mcp` package invokes a predeclared tool over a client path; it is not a canonical server manager and does not discover `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, or `resources/list`.
- `dag-node-mcp-tool` contains a separate official-SDK HTTP/stdio precedent. Agent product packages must not depend on the DAG product; a shared lower client seam is required.
- `agent-transport-mcp` exposes Robota as an MCP server—the opposite direction, owned by #1986.

## Corrections to the original snapshot

- `agent-tool-mcp` is currently `private: true`; the original statement that both packages publish is false.
- TOOL-006 is complete: PR #2040 / commit `a432cd38042f9f07b74999855be50dde15956362` made `MCPTool` and `RelayMcpTool` implement `IToolWithEventService` and added a registrability test. Its Task record remaining `todo` is lifecycle drift owned by #2186, not an MCP blocker.
- The original default-tool count is stale and is not an acceptance criterion.
- Workspace/package dependency claims must say **deployable product/workspace packages**, because `scratch/package.json` is a non-product consumer.
- The linked reference changes frequently. HTTP remains the standard recommended remote path; SSE is deprecated compatibility; WebSocket is a product-specific/custom compatibility decision. Every moving-reference line requires an adopted/adapted/rejected (AAR) decision before implementation.

## Approved architecture placement

- Reclassify/rename the private `agent-tool-mcp` package into a shared lower MCP client package, or replace it and migrate/remove the old package explicitly.
- The shared package owns official-SDK protocol mechanics, transport ports, capability catalogs, provenance, and supervision.
- `agent-framework` owns generic dynamic-tool/session and workspace-authority ports, not MCP policy.
- Provider packages own provider-specific schema projection strategies behind a provider-neutral contract.
- `agent-command` owns `/mcp` metadata and typed effects.
- `agent-cli` only composes the concrete manager and renders generic command results.
- DAG and agent products remain sibling consumers of the shared lower seam.

Because several children share package, catalog, and state-machine contracts, their first Task conversion must establish an `AGREEMENT` Task with a paired spec document before independent implementation Tasks diverge.

## Cause decomposition

### New child issues

2. **P0 — #2520:** project/plugin activation trust and approval
3. **P0 — #2521:** shared MCP client foundation + Streamable HTTP product vertical slice

- **#1990:** tool search plus model/search visibility for a failed MCP server. #2523 produces the canonical failed state; #1990 alone owns its model/search projection.

Separate roots that are not absorbed: #1986 (MCP server direction), #2186 (stale Task lifecycle), #2153 (cross-platform external-payload handles), and #2161 (bounded child-process stream retention).

issue.title: [initiative] Expose Robota sessions as a secure MCP server product mode

parentSnapshots.body:
## Executive verdict

Robota can already expose an embedded session through the public `agent-transport-mcp` SDK package, but `agent-cli` cannot launch a carrier-owning MCP server product mode. This is a **broad P0 parent initiative**, not one executable Task. Independent depth triage and proposal review approved five cause children plus reuse of the existing exact-transport binding chain.

Revalidated against `origin/develop` `f14b164ba7ef402458f0cf08c69ff920dce9966c` and current official MCP/Claude Code documentation on 2026-08-29.

## Current observed state

- `@robota-sdk/agent-transport-mcp` is public and implemented. `createAgentMcpServer()` exposes `submit` and filtered `command_*` tools to an embedding host.
- Direct command calls are rechecked for `modelInvocable` and attributed as `remote` before `executeCommand`; prior remote-admission work is real and must be preserved.
- No deployable product package depends on `agent-transport-mcp`; `agent-cli` has no `mcp serve` route or carrier wiring.
- `createMcpTransport.start()` creates an MCP `Server` but does not connect a carrier. Current SPEC defines host-owned carrier connection, which is insufficient for a product lifecycle.
- The server does not expose the session's canonical runtime tools, prompts, or resources.
- Framework command projection already registers commands as canonical `robota_command_*` runtime tools. MCP's independent `command_*` catalog duplicates identity and execution path.
- Existing tests cover in-memory submission correlation and remote command admission, but not a real stdio client-to-CLI path, protocol-pure stdout, canonical runtime-tool execution, or carrier readiness.

## Corrections to the original snapshot

- “There is no way to point another MCP host at a Robota agent” is false for SDK embedding; the precise gap is **product reachability and canonical runtime capability exposure**.
- `agent-transport-mcp` publishes; `agent-tool-mcp` is private. The earlier comment saying both publish is stale.
- Current Claude Code docs describe `claude mcp serve` as a stdio server exposing tools and say the calling MCP client owns per-call user confirmation. Robota intentionally retains stronger server-side permission/hook/result enforcement; this is an adaptation, not reference parity.
- MCP tools, prompts, and resources have different control semantics. Robota has a canonical runtime tool registry but no equivalent prompt/resource registries, so the minimum slice explicitly rejects prompt/resource exposure rather than inventing them.

## Approved architecture placement

- `agent-interface-session` owns the provider-neutral runtime-tool list/invoke port.
- `agent-session`/`agent-framework` implement it through the existing permission-wrapped runtime.
- `agent-transport-mcp` owns MCP translation and concrete MCP carrier lifecycle/readiness.
- `agent-cli` owns product-mode selection, composition, cwd/trust posture, process I/O/signals/exit, and bundled delivery.
- `agent-command` does not own `mcp serve`; it is a process mode, not a slash/model command.
- Client-direction issues #2519–#2528 remain separate and are reused only for the bidirectional integration proof.

## Cause decomposition

### New native children

1. **P0 — #2530:** canonical session runtime-tool capability over MCP
2. **P0 — #2531:** carrier-owning `robota mcp serve` stdio product mode
3. **P1 — #2532:** prove one served session can also consume MCP
4. **P2/security — #2533:** authenticated loopback Streamable HTTP hosting and protocol-session mapping
5. **P2/security — #2534:** non-loopback MCP resource-server authorization and admission

### Existing dependency chain reused—do not duplicate

- **P0 #2091:** registry stores already-bound heterogeneous adapters.
- **P0 #2107:** HTTP/MCP adapters bind to exact session ports.
- **P2 #2117:** later removes the broad compatibility aggregate; downstream cleanup, not a blocker for first product reachability.

Approved execution graph:

```text
#2530 ───────┐
             ├─> #2107 ─> #2531 ─> #2532
#2091 ───────┘               └─────> #2533 ─> #2534

#2519 + #2520 + #2521 ─────────────> #2532
#2107 ─────────────────────────────> #2117 (later cleanup)
```

#2091 and #2107 were promoted from P2 to P0 because they now block the approved P0 product architecture. #2091's former blocker #2050 is closed; #2091 is executable.

## Original checklist disposition

| Original requirement | Single owner |
| --- | --- |
| One command starts a stdio MCP server | #2531 |
| Expose the agent's own tools | #2530 |
| Caller-controlled working directory | #2531 |
| Document the served surface | #2531 |
| Preserve permissions server-side | #2530 |
| A served session can also consume MCP | #2532 |
| Decide tools/resources/prompts | #2530 |
| Non-stdio carrier and session addressing | #2533 |
| Authentication for non-stdio hosting | #2534 |

Every checklist item has one owner. Dependencies may consume another issue's contract but must not re-own its policy.

## Security and lifecycle decisions

- Canonical MCP tool invocation preserves permission, hooks, result envelope, truncation, audit/events, cancellation, and noninteractive fail-closed behavior.
- Commands appear only through canonical `robota_command_*`; the prerelease `command_*` duplicate path is removed without a shim.
- `submit` remains only as a documented, collision-safe Robota extension.
- Stdio stdout is protocol-only; diagnostics use stderr/non-stdout sinks.
- The first Streamable HTTP release is loopback-only **and authenticated**, with Host/Origin validation. `Mcp-Session-Id` is a mapping key, never a Robota session ID or credential.
- #2534 blocks every non-loopback HTTP release.

## Required research before implementation

Each child must fetch latest `origin/develop`, revalidate its premises, record adopted/adapted/rejected decisions against current official references, state alternatives, and receive independent proposal approval. Relevant sources:

- [Claude Code MCP server reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)

- [MCP resources specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources)
- [MCP authorization specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization)

## Parent disposition

The five new children are native sub-issues. Existing #2091/#2107 remain native children of #2069 and are linked through dependency relationships instead of being re-parented. Closing #1986 means decomposition is complete, not that MCP server product support is implemented.

parentSnapshots.body:
## What problem should this solve?

Robota is receiving GitHub issues faster than it closes them, while each accepted issue pays substantial duplicated delivery cost before implementation can begin. Under the current operating model, the queue does not converge to zero.

This issue is the canonical, self-contained handoff for the throughput initiative. It is independent of SECURITY-002 / #2082 and must not expand PR #2507.

## Executive verdict

- **Recommended triage: P0 parent initiative.**
- **Ground:** queue inflow exceeds closure in both the original calendar-date snapshot and a fresh exact 168-hour measurement; the dominant fixed cost applies to every raw issue.
- **Highest-impact recommendation:** allow Issue-to-Task conversion, an approved PLAN checkpoint, implementation, and DONE evidence to travel through one ordered topic branch and one PR.
- **Constraint:** preserve fail-closed correctness, independent review, CI, Task/spec auditability, issue writeback, and final merge verification.
- **Do not implement this broad parent directly.** The current issue-to-backlog contract requires a broad initiative to be decomposed by cause into child Issues/Tasks. Link and read back every child, then close this parent with the decomposition comment so it is not selected twice.

The issue carries no priority label at intake because repository policy requires triage before assigning P0/P1/P2. The P0 recommendation above supplies the evidence for that later decision.

## Measurements

### Original audit snapshot — 2026-08-29 Asia/Seoul

- Open issues: **259**
- Issues created in the calendar-date window beginning 2026-08-22: **350** (**50/day**)
- Issues closed in that window: **97** (**13.9/day**)
- Net growth: **+253/week** (**+36.1/day**)
- At that inflow, time to zero is unbounded.
- If inflow stopped immediately, 259 issues at 13.9 closures/day would still take about **18.7 days** at the repository-wide recent rate.

The original report described this as “last 7 days”; the exact query used a date boundary. That distinction is now explicit so later measurements do not compare a calendar-date window with an exact rolling window.

### Exact rolling-window revalidation — 2026-08-29 19:58 KST

Window: 2026-08-22T10:58:25Z through 2026-08-29T10:58:25Z.

- Open issues: **264**
- Created in the exact prior 168 hours: **221** (**31.6/day**)
- Closed in the exact prior 168 hours: **90** (**12.9/day**)
- Net growth: **+131/week** (**+18.7/day**)
- With inflow present, the queue still cannot reach zero.
- If inflow stopped, 264 issues at 12.9 closures/day would take about **20.5 days**.

The two windows use different boundaries but reach the same decision: inflow materially exceeds closure. Future reporting must print the window start/end and timezone.

### SECURITY-002 / #2082 direct measurement

- Conversion run started: **2026-08-29 17:08:21 KST**
- Conversion PR #2501 opened: **2026-08-29 17:20:01 KST**
- Conversion PR #2501 merged: **2026-08-29 17:31:35 KST**
- Conversion start to merge: **23m 14s**
- PR open to merge: **11m 34s**
- Conversion PR content: **2 files, +90/-0 lines** — Task and ledger only
- Remote check contexts currently reported for #2501: **25**
- #2501 scans job: **4m 23s**
- Additional implementation-branch pre-source work: **14m+**
- Observed interval before the throughput audit: **44m 48s**
- Runtime source changes during that interval: **0**
- Estimated procedure/recovery share: **about 71%**
- develop advanced by five commits during the pre-implementation ceremony, adding synchronization risk.

Authoritative remote evidence:

- Conversion PR: https://github.com/woojubb/robota/pull/2501
- Merge commit: https://github.com/woojubb/robota/commit/5889201b069d339190ce35e749985934dce90866
- Scans job: https://github.com/woojubb/robota/actions/runs/33242897689/job/99075179334
- Measurement context: https://github.com/woojubb/robota/issues/2082#issuecomment-5461461903

The conversion-start timestamp, pre-source interval, and 71% estimate came from the originating session timeline. The PR timestamps, files, lines, check count, scan duration, and merge commit were re-read from GitHub.

## Corroboration and evidence quality

Three independent subagent audits in the originating session converged on the same qualitative conclusion: the dominant cost was duplicated PR lifecycle, serial gates, repeated evidence, and review/CI round trips rather than decoder implementation. Their detailed transcripts were synthesized into the local report but were not committed as independent repository artifacts, so this convergence is corroboration, not the sole proof.

Evidence strength is intentionally separated:

- GitHub PR timestamps, files, line counts, checks, run durations, issue counts, and merge commit are remotely re-readable.
- Repository rule/skill claims are pinned to the develop commit named below and must be revalidated before work.
- Session timeline values and the 71% estimate are explicitly labelled session-derived.
- Future completion claims must use repeatable commands and before/after measurements, not the originating session narrative.

## Current mechanism at develop f220a879d

The mechanism was revalidated against origin/develop commit f220a879d487c9db1c1e46fe98267a40341f0220.

1. **Conversion and implementation are separated.**
   - Owner: .agents/skills/issue-to-backlog/SKILL.md, “Do not”
   - It says not to start the work in the same change as conversion.
2. **The active backlog must merge before the next begins.**
   - Owner: .agents/rules/backlog-execution.md, “One-Backlog-At-A-Time Rule”
   - Completion includes PR merge into develop and ancestry verification.
3. **Source implementation requires a planning checkpoint first.**
   - Owner: .agents/rules/backlog-execution.md, “Pre-implementation planning checkpoint”
   - The checkpoint must be an earlier ancestor and is already mechanically checked.
4. **Feature work must use a feature branch and PR to develop.**
   - Owner: .agents/rules/git-branch.md, “Branch Policy”
5. **Read-only exploration is allowed before mutation.**
   - Owner: .agents/skills/user-request-gate/SKILL.md
   - This is the existing safe seam for hiding remote wait without concurrent implementation.
6. **A broad issue is not one Task by default.**
   - Owner: .agents/skills/issue-to-backlog/SKILL.md, “Boundary decision”
   - Split by cause and independent verification, not by package or deliverable count.

The core amendment should move the stopping boundary: refuse source implementation before conversion and PLAN are valid ancestors, but do not require the conversion itself to have already paid a separate merged PR lifecycle.

## Ranked bottlenecks

### P0 — Two complete PR lifecycles per raw issue

A typical raw issue pays once for Issue-to-Task conversion and again for implementation. CI, automated review, merge evidence, merge verification, and develop synchronization are duplicated. On #2082, eliminating the separate conversion PR would have avoided at least the measured 11m 34s remote wait and roughly 20–30 minutes of the full conversion lifecycle.

### P0 — Intake exceeds closure

The exact rolling window is growing by 131 issues/week. Workflow optimization alone is insufficient unless closure exceeds intake or audit-driven filing is bounded. Blockers, security, and data-correctness findings must still be filed immediately; non-blocking manifestations should be deduplicated and grouped by root cause.

### P1 — Useful wait is serialized

The one-backlog rule prevents starting another implementation while CI/review runs. That safety property can remain while read-only preflight for the next disjoint issue is used systematically: dependency/blocker inspection, source inventory, duplicate/premise checks, and prospective lane/owner identification.

### P1 — The same evidence is owned repeatedly

Approach, architecture, affected files, tests, scenario disposition, and verdict are copied through Task, recommendation, spec, PLAN/DONE evidence, PR body, and loop ledgers. Repeated prose creates synchronization, review, and drift cost without adding an independent fact owner.

Relevant owners include:

- .agents/rules/backlog-execution.md — Recommendation Gate and PR Unit Rule
- .agents/templates/mini-spec-template.md
- .agents/specs/gate-catalogue.md
- Task and spec document contracts

### P1 — Pre-implementation roles form a serial critical path

A normal L1 code item can require, in order:

1. finding-depth triage
2. recommendation authoring
3. independent proposal review and possible revision
4. user-execution scenario applicability decision
5. L1 spec approval and PLAN judgment
6. dedicated planning-checkpoint commit
7. TDD implementation

Independent review is not the waste: SECURITY-002 proposal review found four real design defects. The target is duplicated evidence and preventable serialization around valuable review.

### P1 — Findings amplify into full remote round trips

A remote finding can require a reply, depth disposition, thread resolution, local review, push, and a fresh full CI/review cycle. Repository evidence cited by the original audit records 38 review rounds across five PRs at roughly 6–10 minutes per round. The git-branch rule documents PR #2323 spending roughly 4h 40m in the loop while changing no non-comment TypeScript line after the first commit.

This is a measured constraint for the redesign: do not remove review, but avoid creating unnecessary new heads and reuse verification safely.

### P1 — Loop-run runtime and scan semantics disagree

The runtime refuses a same-day successor when an OPEN run exists, while the scan tolerates OPEN records for seven days. A green merged orphan can block later work.

Existing child defect — do not duplicate:

- #2504: https://github.com/woojubb/robota/issues/2504
- scripts/harness/loop-run.mjs
- scripts/harness/scan-loop-run-records.mjs

### P2 — Verification repeats over unchanged or nearly unchanged trees

Targeted TDD, source-changing commit verification, post-implementation verification, pre-push CI-equivalent verification, and remote CI overlap. Final-clean-HEAD receipts exist as a seam, but identity and reuse are not consistently maximized.

## Required cause decomposition

The executor must revalidate this map with issue-to-backlog and finding-depth before authoring Tasks. It is an initial cause map, not permission to copy six placeholder Tasks.

1. **P0 — Combined conversion + PLAN + implementation lifecycle**
   - Cause: conversion is required to be a separate completed change, although planning order is already mechanically enforceable.
2. **P0 — Intake stabilization + throughput measurement**
   - Cause: filing has no bounded policy tied to measured net growth.
3. **P1 — Safe read-only overlap during remote waits**
   - Cause: allowed read-only work is not made a normal, explicit preflight path.
4. **P1 — Evidence ownership and reference-only projections**
   - Cause: the same facts are copied into several independently edited artifacts.
5. **P1 — Transactional loop-run lifecycle**
   - Existing external owner: #2504. Link it; do not file a duplicate.
6. **P2 — Verification receipt identity and DAG execution**
   - Cause: unchanged final-tree evidence is recomputed and independent stages are not maximally parallelized.

Review-round amplification and the serial pre-implementation role chain are cross-cutting measurements. Create another child only if depth triage proves an independent cause not owned by lanes 1, 4, or 6.

Under the current issue-to-backlog rule, causes needing separate priority, ownership, or terminal disposition become child Issues. After all child links are posted and read back, close #2512 with a decomposition comment; the children carry execution. If several internal Tasks share one boundary, create an AGREEMENT Task/spec pair as required by the same skill.

## Observable outcomes and acceptance criteria

### A — One PR with an enforced planning prelude

- A raw triaged P0/P1 issue can move from conversion through implementation and DONE evidence in one topic branch and one PR.
- Commit order is mechanically enforced:
  1. atomic Issue-to-Task conversion commit
  2. approved PLAN checkpoint commit
  3. implementation commits
  4. DONE/completion commit
- Source changes are refused unless conversion finalization and PLAN are earlier ancestors.
- Issue Task-marker write/read-back and priority-label removal finish before source implementation.
- Existing Task/spec, independent recommendation review, scenario decision, CI, review, and develop merge auditability remain intact.
- A regression test proves retrospective conversion and retrospective PLAN are rejected.
- A measured representative issue pays one remote PR lifecycle, not two.
- The amendment changes the owning rule and its mechanical checks together; it does not create a prose-only exception.

### B — Stabilize intake and publish net-growth measurement

- One owner command/dashboard reports open count plus created, closed, and net counts for an explicit rolling window.
- Output includes start, end, timezone, query semantics, and the repository so two windows cannot be confused.
- Agent/automated audits use a bounded filing policy for non-blocking findings.
- Duplicate and root-cause grouping is checked before child issue creation.
- Blockers, security, and data-correctness findings remain immediate-file exceptions.
- A threshold and stop/slow action for positive net growth are defined and mechanically reachable.
- The initiative records a negative rolling seven-day net count as the target outcome.

### C — Hide remote wait without concurrent implementation

- While the active PR is pending CI/review, the next disjoint issue may receive read-only dependency, blocker, source-location, duplicate, premise, lane, and owner preflight.
- No second implementation branch is opened and no files for that issue are edited.
- The active PR remains the only mutable delivery unit.
- The workflow names the preflight artifact or output so the next session can reuse it without treating it as implementation authorization.
- Tests or a mechanical guard distinguish permitted read-only preflight from forbidden concurrent mutation.

### D — Remove duplicate evidence ownership

Define one owner per fact:

- Task: problem, scope, issue linkage, lifecycle status
- Spec: accepted design, alternatives, affected files, completion criteria, test plan
- PR: links plus concise diff and verification summary
- Gate/loop ledger: machine result and subject identity only

Acceptance:

- Non-owner artifacts reference the owner instead of copying long prose.
- A mechanical check detects stale or contradictory projections where feasible.
- Existing audit trails remain readable; migration is prospective or uses explicit historical containment rather than fabricated evidence.
- A measured representative work unit writes materially less duplicate prose without losing an acceptance criterion or verdict.

### E — Make loop runs transactional (#2504)

- A newly introduced unbound OPEN run cannot cross the commit/merge boundary.
- A genuinely live local owner can continue its run.
- Runtime open refusal and the loop-run-records scan agree on validity.
- An open/round/close wrapper cannot leave an orphan on ordinary success, failure, or interruption.
- Recovery is subject-bound and does not silently abandon another owner’s run.
- Dedicated tests reproduce the merged-orphan case from #2504 and prove the successor can open after valid recovery.

### F — Reuse final-tree verification receipts and parallelize the verification DAG

- Targeted tests run during RED/GREEN; the full CI-equivalent suite runs once on the final clean HEAD.
- A receipt is reusable only when commit identity and every relevant input identity match.
- Any relevant source, config, dependency, toolchain, or gate-definition change invalidates reuse.
- Pre-push reports whether it reused a receipt and why.
- Independent verification stages run in parallel where their dependency graph permits.
- Tests prove a stale or partial receipt cannot produce a false green.
- Before/after wall time and duplicated-stage counts are measured.

### Initiative-level completion

- No correctness, security, independent-review, CI, or merge-verification gate is weakened to achieve speed.
- At least one representative issue is measured end to end before and after the highest-impact amendment.
- Remote PR lifecycles per raw issue fall from two to one for the eligible path.
- The measurement command is repeatable by another session.
- The issue intake/closure trend is reported with explicit windows until the rolling seven-day net becomes negative.
- Residual causes are linked to named child issues rather than silently dropped.

## Immediate optimizations that require no rule amendment

These can be used while the initiative is being decomposed, without starting concurrent implementation:

- Load only the skill needed for the current phase.
- Run independent source inventory and depth research in parallel where delegation is permitted.
- Finish local Round A review before opening the PR.
- Use targeted tests during implementation and run full verification on the final clean commit.
- Run loop-run show before opening a new loop.
- After a merge command or failure, re-read PR state, mergedAt, head, and base before recovery. PR #2501 was already server-merged while recovery work began.
- During CI/review waits, perform only read-only preflight for the next disjoint issue.
- Reuse an existing valid receipt only when its identity check passes; never infer reuse from a similar diff.

## Non-goals and guardrails

- Do not remove or bypass tests, independent proposal review, automated review, review-thread resolution, or final merge verification.
- Do not authorize two concurrently mutable implementation branches.
- Do not mix this work into PR #2507 or any unrelated active issue branch.
- Do not rewrite historical transcript or ledger evidence to make scans appear clean.
- Do not duplicate #2504.
- Do not treat faster runners alone as completion.
- Do not treat intake throttling alone as completion.
- Do not implement directly from this broad parent without cause decomposition and the required recommendation/amendment gates.
- Do not assume the 2026-08-29 branch/HEAD snapshot is still current.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep conversion and implementation as separate PRs.** Preserves present sequencing but necessarily pays two remote lifecycles per issue and failed the measured throughput need.
- **Remove independent review or test gates.** Rejected. SECURITY-002 review found real defects; correctness controls are valuable.
- **Only add faster CI runners.** Reduces individual duration but not duplicated lifecycle, evidence, synchronization, or serialization.
- **Only reduce intake.** Necessary but does not address the measured procedure/recovery share for accepted work.
- **Allow parallel implementation branches.** Rejected for this initiative; safe overlap is read-only preflight while one delivery unit remains mutable.
- **Patch #2082 inline.** Rejected because frontmatter decoding and repository-wide delivery policy have different owners, risks, and verification scopes.
- **Create one monolithic throughput Task.** Rejected by the current cause-based Issue-to-Task contract; the lanes have different owners and independent completion decisions.

## Recommended execution order

1. Triage #2512 as the parent initiative and perform cause/dependency/depth classification.
2. Create and read back the child Issue links; reuse #2504 for the transactional loop lane.
3. Land **A: combined conversion + planning prelude + implementation PR amendment** first.
4. Land **B: intake stabilization and net-growth measurement**.
5. Complete **#2504 / transactional loop runs**.
6. Land **D: evidence ownership deduplication**.
7. Adopt **C: safe read-only overlap** immediately where current rules already allow it; add mechanism only where the audit shows one is missing.
8. Land **F: receipt reuse and verification DAG parallelization**.
9. Re-measure the same metrics and record residual children.

Delivery remains sequential unless the latest rules explicitly authorize otherwise; read-only audit/research can overlap.

## Reproduction commands


```bash

printf 'window-start=%s\n' "$throughput_since"

gh api -X GET search/issues \
  -f q="repo:woojubb/robota is:issue created:>=$throughput_since" \
```


Before authoring any child or amendment, read the latest versions of:

Then run the required recommendation and amendment gates on a separate compliant branch or worktree cut from freshly fetched origin/develop. Preserve existing stashes and unrelated working-tree state.

- No standalone open issue described this combined initiative. Search hits came from the former temporary #2082 comment.

## Where agent-cli stands

`packages/agent-core/src/permissions/permission-gate.ts:129` defines `primaryArg()`, and line 189 is the only place a pattern is matched against tool arguments. One argument per tool, chosen by the tool's name. A rule cannot say "never spawn a subagent on this model" or "deny writes through this MCP server", and no rule survives `bypassPermissions`.

## Why it matters

This is the seam every other safety feature attaches to. MCP tool gating, sandboxing, and any classifier-based mode all need to express a rule about something other than one positional argument.

## What Claude Code implements — gate checklist

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions

**Rule shapes**
- [ ] `Tool` with no parentheses matches every use; `Tool(*)` is equivalent
- [ ] A bare-name **deny** rule removes the tool from the model's context entirely, rather than failing at call time
- [ ] `Tool(specifier)` for the tool's own primary content, with per-tool syntax (`Bash(npm run build)`, `Read(./.env)`, `WebFetch(domain:example.com)`)
- [ ] **`Tool(param:value)` matches any top-level input parameter** — deny and ask rules only, because an allow rule keyed to one parameter would not establish that the whole call is safe
- [ ] Parameter matching rules that are all separately checkable: direct fields only (nothing nested); one parameter per rule; `*` wildcard in the value; an **omitted** parameter never matches, so `Tool(p:*)` does not match a call that leaves `p` unset; the value is compared **before normalization**, against exactly what the model sent; whitespace around the colon ignored
- [ ] The primary content field is **excluded** from parameter matching by name (`command`, `file_path`, `path`, `url`, …) because such a rule would be trivially bypassable — and a rule that tries it is ignored **with a startup warning**, not silently
- [ ] Glob patterns in the **tool-name** position for deny and ask rules, e.g. one rule denying every MCP tool
- [ ] Trailing-wildcard equivalence (`Bash(ls:*)` ≡ `Bash(ls *)`), with the colon form recognized only at the end

**Precedence and modes**
- [ ] Three verbs, not two: `allow`, `ask`, `deny`
- [ ] **Deny rules apply in every mode, including the bypass mode; allow rules have no effect in the bypass mode**
- [ ] A documented set of actions **no mode auto-approves**: anything matched by an ask rule, tools that require user interaction, removals targeting critical paths, and cross-session-messaging safeguards
- [ ] Protected paths that are never auto-approved outside the bypass mode
- [ ] Settings-file scopes with a stated precedence, and rules that are checked into the repo to be shared
- [ ] A command that shows the effective rules and recent denials

**Tool-specific rule semantics**
- [ ] Compound shell commands are decomposed, so a rule cannot be evaded by chaining
- [ ] A built-in read-only command set that does not prompt
- [ ] Redirections considered as part of the command's effect
- [ ] gitignore-style path rules for read and edit
- [ ] Directory scoping: file access can be widened to additional directories, and that widening explicitly does **not** widen configuration trust

## How to read the checklist

The checklist is **what Claude Code actually implements**, read from its product documentation on 2026-08-22 — it is the gate list for this issue, not a copy order. Robota is multi-provider and open-source; some lines will not apply, and some deserve a better answer than Anthropic's. But every line must be **explicitly decided**: adopted, adapted, or rejected with a reason. An implementation that silently skips a line has not met this gate.

## Research before implementing — mandatory

**This issue is a gap and a candidate, not a design and not an approval. Do not start writing code from it.**

Before implementation, a research pass must be recorded in the work item that carries this forward:

1. **Re-read the reference behaviour from the linked documentation** — it moves weekly, and the checklist below is a snapshot. Confirm each line still holds, and note what changed.
2. **Establish the provider-neutral form.** A design that only works against Anthropic is not a design — say what each supported provider maps onto, and what a provider without an equivalent does instead.
3. **Survey what this repo already has** so the change extends an existing seam instead of adding a parallel one.
4. **Walk the checklist and record a verdict per line**, then **state the alternatives considered and why the chosen one wins**, and get a reviewer sign-off before implementation starts.

Only once that research is written down does implementation begin.

This issue says *"no rule survives `bypassPermissions`."* CORE-025 landed since, and `packages/agent-session/src/permission-enforcer.ts:162-177` resolves a policy **before** the session-mode gate:

```ts
// CORE-025: a background/subagent task permission policy is resolved BEFORE the session-mode gate, so
// `deny`/`preapproved`/`inherit-allowlist` override even a permissive mode (e.g. bypassPermissions).
if (this.permissionPolicy) {
  const policyDecision = resolvePermissionByPolicy(…);
  if (policyDecision === 'allow') return true;

```

| | state |
|---|---|

## Summary

One user-visible command is currently declared twice: `ICommand` is used for discovery/palette/transport projection, while `ISystemCommand` is used for execution. Command modules therefore repeat identity and policy metadata, and the two registries can disagree.

This is not a compatibility-preservation request. These interfaces have not had a stable release, so the end state should replace them directly rather than add another adapter or deprecated facade.

## Evidence

- [`ICommand` is an optional-heavy union-by-convention](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-interface-transport/src/command-contracts.ts#L20-L60), combining palette fields, executable closures, skill metadata, plugin provenance, and two model-invocation flags.
- [`ISystemCommand` separately repeats command identity and policy](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-framework/src/command-api/contracts.ts#L30-L53).
- [`ICommandModule` carries parallel command-source and system-command arrays](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-framework/src/command-api/command-module.ts#L8-L18).
- [The built-in projection manually copies only a subset of fields](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-framework/src/commands/builtin-source.ts#L7-L17); `displayName` and `example` are already omitted there.
- Production command modules contain paired entry/system factories, and the framework previously needed a second projection fix after model-invocation metadata drift exposed operator-only commands (#1872).
- `ICommand.execute?` is not the production execution seam; [`SystemCommandExecutor` invokes `ISystemCommand.execute`](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-framework/src/commands/system-command-executor.ts#L86-L92).

## Proposed direction

Create one owner for a discriminated `CommandDefinition` (`builtin | skill | plugin`). Keep the executable definition separate from its serializable descriptor, derive palette/transport/model-capability projections from the same definition, and remove competing positive/negative invocation flags.

## Acceptance criteria

- A command's name, presentation metadata, safety, permission, and invocation policy have one source of truth.
- Executable variants require a handler; data-only descriptors cannot carry functions.
- Command modules no longer register paired entry/system objects.
- Model, remote, palette, and executor paths consume projections from the same definition.
- Type and functional tests prove a restricted command cannot become invocable through projection loss.
- `ICommand`/`ISystemCommand` compatibility shims are not retained.

## Non-duplication

#2052 addresses duplicate declarations, export-star barrels, and pass-through types in general. This issue addresses the runtime model in which every command instance is deliberately defined twice and can carry contradictory policy.

## Summary

Skill and agent definition files cross a filesystem/plugin trust boundary through two permissive hand-written frontmatter parsers. Both cast partial records to typed contracts, silently ignore malformed lines/unknown keys, and accept values that violate downstream invariants.

This surface is prerelease. Define the correct schema now; do not retain permissive parsing for legacy compatibility.

## Evidence

- [The skill parser declares another local metadata interface](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-framework/src/commands/skill-source.ts#L9-L20) rather than consuming an owner schema.
- [Boolean values are parsed as `rawValue === 'true'`](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-framework/src/commands/skill-source.ts#L43-L70), so `disable-model-invocation: treu` becomes `false` and widens model authority instead of failing.
- [`context`, `model`, and `effort` are copied as unconstrained strings](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-framework/src/commands/skill-source.ts#L73-L96).
- [Execution recognizes only the exact `context === 'fork'`](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-framework/src/commands/skill-executor.ts#L86-L113); other values silently become inject mode. Production does not consume the parsed skill `model`/`effort` fields.
- [Agent files use a second parser and `parseInt` before a cast](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-framework/src/agents/agent-definition-loader.ts#L39-L83), accepting numeric prefixes and `NaN` for `maxTurns`.

## Proposed direction

Create one owner-owned decoder for skill/agent definition metadata with explicit variants and field-path diagnostics. Use a closed context union, strict booleans, a positive finite integer for `maxTurns`, and the model-effort SSOT. Reject unsupported keys or report them visibly. Remove unused fields unless they are implemented end to end.

## Acceptance criteria

- Boolean typos, invalid context, invalid `maxTurns`, and wrong field types fail with file/path diagnostics.
- Native, `.agents`, Claude-compatible, and plugin discovery paths use the same decoder semantics.
- `model` and `effort` are either honored end to end or removed from the contract.
- Unknown fields have an explicit reject/warn policy and are never silently cast.
- A malformed disabling flag can never make a skill model-invocable.

#1987 includes the product feature of reasoning effort. This issue owns boundary decoding and invalid metadata behavior across all skill/agent fields.

## Summary

There is no stable persistence compatibility requirement. Introduce one versioned contract and reject malformed/unsupported data rather than preserving permissive readers.

## Evidence

- [`IInteractiveSessionRecord` is TypeScript-only despite being persisted and transferred](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-interface-transport/src/session-contracts.ts#L447-L482).
- [`SessionStore.load/list` JSON-parse and cast](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-session/src/session-store.ts#L92-L133); syntax/read failures are treated as missing/skip and parseable wrong nested shapes are accepted.
- [The artifact decoder validates envelope version plus only an object/id-shaped record](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-session/src/session-artifact.ts#L58-L81).

## Proposed direction

Let the session contract owner provide versioned `decodeInteractiveSessionRecord`, artifact-envelope, and event-name-discriminated JSONL codecs. ## Summary

Command/HTTP executor timeout, spawn, HTTP, parse, and unsupported-executor outcomes become a non-0/non-2 exit code or an `unknownHookType`, and the runner/helper continue without blocking `PreToolUse`. Prompt/agent hook types can also be accepted by configuration without the CLI wiring their required factories.

- [Command hook failures collapse to exit code 1](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-core/src/hooks/executors/command-executor.ts#L52-L76); [HTTP/network/parse failures do the same](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-core/src/hooks/executors/http-executor.ts#L41-L70).
- [The HTTP response is bare-cast and checks `ok` by truthiness](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-core/src/hooks/executors/http-executor.ts#L57-L67), so `{ "ok": "false" }` is treated as allow.
- [HookRunner only gives special meaning to exit 0 and 2 and records unsupported types](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-core/src/hooks/hook-runner.ts#L156-L180).
- [The session helper checks only `blocked`](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-session/src/tool-hook-helpers.ts#L57-L77), so error/unknown outcomes allow the tool.

## Summary

The DAG file import adapter is only a shallow format discriminator, not the total decoder its typed return contract implies. Parseable JSON with missing or wrong nested fields can pass as `IDagDefinition` and crash command paths before semantic validation can report useful diagnostics.

No legacy compatibility is required: fully decode the accepted disk formats and reject all malformed variants.

## Evidence

- [Workflow/legacy guards check only top-level arrays/version or `dagId` plus `nodes`](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/dag-builder/src/dag-workflow-converter.ts#L294-L310).
- [`parseDagFileContent` uses those predicates to return `IDagDefinition`](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/dag-builder/src/parsed-dag-file.ts#L55-L71).
- [The canonical type requires version/status/nodes/edges and nested node/edge contracts](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/dag-core/src/types/domain.ts#L97-L109).
- [The semantic validator assumes typed strings/arrays and calls methods directly](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/dag-core/src/services/definition-validator.ts#L13-L40).
- [`/workflows validate` immediately iterates definition edges](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-command-workflows/src/validate-command.ts#L47-L78), so a shallowly accepted legacy object can throw instead of yielding validation errors.

## Proposed direction

Make the DAG-builder boundary perform three explicit stages: total decode of each disk format with field-path diagnostics, conversion to the canonical definition, then semantic validation. The semantic validator should continue to accept only decoded domain values.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every required top-level and nested node/edge field is decoded before returning `IDagDefinition`.
- Wrong primitives, missing fields, extra/unsupported variants, and malformed nested structures return typed path diagnostics, never `TypeError`.
- All DAG file readers use the same codec.
- Property/fuzz and command-level tests cover both supported disk formats.
- No bare `as IDagDefinition` remains at a JSON boundary.

Model tool-call arguments are checked for JSON syntax but not for the required non-null object root before being cast to `TToolParameters`. `null`, scalars, or arrays can reach validators that assume a record and abort request/batch construction instead of becoming one tool's typed failure.

This provider boundary is prerelease. Enforce the actual contract directly rather than accommodate malformed shapes.

## Evidence

- [`TToolParameters` is a record contract](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-core/src/interfaces/types.ts#L62-L65).
- [Tool arguments are `JSON.parse`d and cast without root validation](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-core/src/services/tool-execution-service.ts#L191-L219).
- [Parameter validation uses `field in parameters` and object enumeration](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-core/src/services/parameter-validator.ts#L103-L136), which assumes a non-null object.
- [Execution builds the request batch before per-tool execution/error isolation](https://github.com/woojubb/robota/blob/15800bf0f0023406cf06981a7afcc2cfdcd17f63/packages/agent-core/src/services/execution-round-tools.ts#L82-L105), so one malformed call can interrupt otherwise valid calls.

Add an owner `decodeToolCallArguments(callId, name, unknown)` that accepts only non-null, non-array JSON objects, then invoke the existing schema validator. Convert parse/root/schema errors into that call's typed tool failure and continue independent calls according to batch policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- Malformed JSON, `null`, scalar, and array roots become typed failures for the corresponding call.
- Valid calls in the same batch still execute under `continueOnError` semantics.
- Error payloads preserve call id, tool name, and actionable decode details.
- The owner decoder is used by every provider/tool-call ingress.
- Mixed-batch functional tests cover every invalid root shape.

CORE-039 covers tool-schema subset semantics; #2045 covers transport messages and #2047 subagent IPC. This issue is the provider tool-call argument boundary.

**Measurement at `3a3f4d80c`, and it changes the shape of the proposal: the decoder this issue asks for already exists — in one provider, private, and correct.**

## Every site that decodes tool-call arguments

Thirteen references to `function.arguments` across the workspace; six pass the string through untouched (openai, openai-compatible, qwen adapters) and three use it for display text. **Four actually decode it, and no two behave the same:**

| site | parses | root guard | on failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-provider-gemini/src/gemini/request-converter.ts:200` | yes | **yes** | throws a named error |
| `agent-core/src/services/tool-execution-service.ts:204` | yes | **no** — cast to `TToolParameters` | `ValidationError`, aborts the batch |
| `agent-provider-anthropic/src/anthropic/message-converter.ts:79` | yes | **no** — no cast at all | **nothing catches it** |
| `agent-transport-tui/src/utils/tool-call-extractor.ts:65` | yes | **no** — cast to `Record<…>` | swallowed, `catch {}` |

## The guard this issue specifies is already written

`request-converter.ts:200`, private to that file:

```ts
function parseToolCallArguments(serializedArguments: string): IGoogleJsonObject {
  const parsedArguments = JSON.parse(serializedArguments) as TGoogleJsonValue;
  if (!isJsonObject(parsedArguments)) {
    throw new Error('Google provider tool call arguments must be a JSON object.');
  }
  return parsedArguments;
}

function isJsonObject(value: TGoogleJsonValue): value is IGoogleJsonObject {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}
```

`typeof === 'object' && !== null && !Array.isArray` **is** the non-null non-array object root the acceptance criteria describe. So `decodeToolCallArguments` is not a new invariant to invent — it is **this function, promoted out of one provider and given the typed-failure conversion the issue asks for.** That is a materially smaller and lower-risk change than the issue's wording implies, and it comes with the argument already settled: someone hit this, decided the root must be an object, and wrote the check.

## One site is worse than the issue records

The issue says malformed input "can reach validators that assume a record and abort request/batch construction." At `message-converter.ts:79` it does not get that far:

```ts
input: JSON.parse(tc.function.arguments),
```

**No cast, no root check, and no `try` anywhere above it in the function.** A malformed argument string from the model throws straight out of Anthropic message conversion — not a `ValidationError`, not one tool's typed failure, and not attributable to a call id. The issue's evidence list does not include this site.

And the TUI site is the mirror image: `catch { /* ignore parse errors */ }`. Same contract, four sites, and the two extremes are *throw uncatchably* and *silently ignore*.

## What this does to the acceptance criteria

> *The owner decoder is used by every provider/tool-call ingress.*

That criterion is the whole issue, and it is now measurable rather than aspirational: **four sites, listed above, and the count is a check somebody can write.** Worth saying plainly that a list of four names four values — coverage is about every path that produces a decoded argument object, and the six pass-through sites need a decision recorded too, even if the decision is "these never decode, so they are out of scope."

## Unchanged

The core defect is fully intact at today's head — `tool-execution-service.ts:204` casts a bare `JSON.parse` result to `TToolParameters`, and grepping the file for any guard returns zero. Every acceptance criterion is unmet.

## Not started

Measured only. This still reaches a design — an owner module, its placement, and the batch-policy interaction — so it needs a spec document before implementation, and `parameter-validator.ts` having moved from `services/` to `tool-registry/` makes the placement a live question rather than a settled one.

That changes what "done" means. A per-site fix closes an issue; it does not close the class. channel-frames.ts:141   decodeChannelFrame   total, returns { ok, error }, checks length/version/bounds
```
request-converter.ts:200 parseToolCallArguments  non-null non-array object root  (private to gemini)
pairing-frames.ts:32    isEnrollFrame        reads one field  (beside two guards that read none)
```

Recording the size, not arguing for a sweep. A 50-site change touching 45 files across five packages is the largest possible conflict surface, and this repository already learned that on issue #2251, which split by rule for exactly that reason. **The useful output here is the number and the fact that three correct implementations already exist** — whoever designs the fix should know both before choosing its shape.

comments.author: woojubb
comments.body:
**Part of this is already delivered by adjacent work. Measured at `8139f8458`.**

This issue asks for *"Node filesystem repository implementations"* with *"atomic/permission-aware persistence"*, behind application ports.

```
packages/agent-cli/src/remote-control/host-identity.ts        writeOwnerOnlyFile: 2 uses
packages/agent-cli/src/remote-control/trusted-device-store.ts writeOwnerOnlyFile: 2 uses

repository ports (interface I…Repository / RepositoryPort) anywhere:  0
```

**The permission-aware half arrived from SEC-020** (issue #2021), which moved every writer into the CLI's own store onto `writeOwnerOnlyFile` — the helper that creates the parent owner-only and sets the file mode at creation rather than chmod-ing after. Both files this issue names are on it.

`trusted-device-store.ts` also carries a note that its corruption behaviour was deliberately aligned with `settings-io`'s `SettingsParseError` — so the *decoder* half has a stated model too, even without the tests this issue asks for.

**So what remains is the port, not the persistence.** The acceptance criterion *"The application package imports only repository ports"* is untouched: **zero repository interfaces exist anywhere in the tree.**

## Why the split matters to whoever takes it

Read as written, this is "write Node adapters with careful persistence and put them behind ports" — two pieces of work. **The careful persistence exists and is already correct**; re-implementing it inside a new adapter would be a regression risk for no gain, and the honest shape of the remaining work is:

1. define the repository ports (none exist),
2. move the two existing files behind them **without changing what they do**.

Step 2 is a relocation with a strong invariant: `writeOwnerOnlyFile` must still be the writer afterwards. Issue #2229 (closed today) is the case for why that invariant is worth stating — the update-check cache was the one file in that store that had been left off the helper, and nothing noticed until someone ran the product and listed the directory.

## And its declared blocker is still open

```
this issue declares : Blocked by: #2105
issue #2105 state    : OPEN  (itself blocked by #2086)
```

Unlike the seven found today whose blockers had all closed, this chain is real — #2086 → #2105 → this. Recorded so the distinction is visible: a stale `Blocked by:` and a live one look identical in an issue body.

Not allocating — measured while surveying the queue.

before.body:
Parent initiative: #2512 (reused as cause E; no duplicate child was filed)

## What happened?

The committed ledger `.agents/loop-runs/backlog-execution-orchestrator.jsonl` contains `r20260829014753` with `closed=null`, `ref=null`, and zero rounds. Running `node scripts/harness/loop-run.mjs open --loop backlog-execution-orchestrator` refuses a new run because the same-day orphan is indistinguishable from a live owner. The loop-run scan still passes because OPEN records are tolerated for seven days.

The state was introduced by commit `cff8ef9c5c79185e4879e8514c23c418c6a9a38a` immediately after DOCS-039 was closed. History also shows the same class in `r20260822101445`, later abandoned. INFRA-136 commit `8a0781208` did not prevent a newly introduced OPEN record from crossing a commit or merge boundary.

## Reproduction

1. Check out `develop` at or after `cff8ef9c5c79185e4879e8514c23c418c6a9a38a`.
2. Run `node scripts/harness/loop-run.mjs open --loop backlog-execution-orchestrator`.
3. Observe refusal naming `r20260829014753`.
4. Run the loop-run-records scan and observe that the merged OPEN record is tolerated.

## Expected behavior

A newly introduced OPEN loop record without terminal closure or subject binding must not cross the commit/PR merge boundary, while a genuinely live local run remains usable by its owner. Runtime refusal and the scan must share the same validity model so a green merged ledger cannot block every successor.

## Recommended priority and cause

**P1.** Make loop runs transactional across ordinary success, failure, interruption, commit, and merge boundaries. This is an independent foundational defect reused by #2512, not part of SECURITY-002/#2082.

## Acceptance criteria

- A newly introduced unbound OPEN run cannot cross the commit or merge boundary.
- A genuinely live local owner can continue its own run without being mistaken for an orphan.
- Runtime open refusal and `loop-run-records` scanning use the same validity semantics.
- An open/round/close wrapper cannot leave an orphan on ordinary success, failure, or interruption.
- Recovery is subject-bound, records its disposition, and cannot silently abandon another owner's run.
- Dedicated tests reproduce the merged-orphan case above and prove a valid successor can open after recovery.
- Existing historical records are contained explicitly; they are not rewritten to manufacture a green history.
- Failures and recovery instructions are visible; no command completes quietly after a ledger error.

## Boundary and duplicate audit

This issue owns transactional loop-run lifecycle only. #2514 owns single-PR conversion/PLAN/implementation; #2515 owns intake metrics; #2516 owns read-only wait overlap; #2517 owns evidence projections; #2518 owns verification receipts. The original #2082 work was correctly kept separate.

## Submission checks

- [x] Existing issue search performed before filing.
- [x] Reused as #2512 cause E rather than filing a duplicate.

Parent initiative: #2512

## Problem

Every eligible raw issue currently pays a complete remote PR lifecycle for Issue-to-Task conversion and then another for implementation. The #2082 measurement recorded 23m 14s from conversion start to merge, including 11m 34s from PR open to merge, before runtime source work began. Repeating CI, review, merge verification, and develop synchronization for metadata-only conversion is the largest fixed cost paid by each accepted issue.

## Recommended priority and cause

**P0.** Move the stopping boundary so conversion and an approved PLAN remain mandatory earlier ancestors, but do not require conversion to merge through a separate PR before implementation starts.

This is a workflow/amendment cause, not permission to weaken review or implement retrospectively. Revalidate the current owners on latest `origin/develop`, including the issue-to-backlog skill, backlog-execution rule, branch rule, planning checkpoint checks, and Task/spec lifecycle.

## Expected behavior

An eligible raw P0/P1 issue can travel through one ordered topic branch and one PR:

1. atomic Issue-to-Task conversion commit
2. approved PLAN checkpoint commit
3. implementation commits
4. DONE/completion commit

The repository must refuse source changes unless conversion finalization and PLAN are valid earlier ancestors.

## Acceptance criteria

- Issue Task-marker write/read-back and priority-label removal complete before source implementation.
- Conversion and PLAN are mechanically required earlier ancestors; retrospective conversion or PLAN is rejected by regression tests.
- Task/spec auditability, independent recommendation review, scenario disposition, CI, automated review, thread resolution, merge verification, and develop ancestry verification remain intact.
- The owning rule/skill and every enforcing hook or scan change together; there is no prose-only exception.
- One representative issue is measured end to end before and after the amendment.
- The eligible path pays one remote PR lifecycle rather than two.
- Failure and recovery behavior is explicit, fail-closed, and does not fabricate historical evidence.

## Non-goals

- Do not allow source implementation before conversion and PLAN.
- Do not remove independent review, tests, CI, or final merge verification.
- Do not authorize two concurrently mutable implementation branches.
- Do not redesign loop-run transactionality here; that is #2504.

## Duplicate and boundary audit

Parent initiative: #2512

## Problem

Issue intake materially exceeds closure, so optimizing individual delivery alone cannot make the queue converge to zero. In the exact 168-hour revalidation recorded in #2512, 221 issues were created and 90 closed: net **+131/week**. The repository also lacks one canonical, repeatable measurement that prints its query window and a bounded filing policy for non-blocking audit findings.

## Recommended priority and cause

**P0.** Establish one owner command/dashboard for throughput and a bounded, root-cause-oriented intake policy. This is urgent because the measured queue grows even while issues are being closed.

## Expected behavior

Operators can reproduce the same open/created/closed/net metrics for an explicit rolling window, and automated audits slow or group non-blocking findings when the queue is growing. Blockers, security, and data-correctness findings remain immediate-file exceptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- One canonical command reports repository, open count, created count, closed count, net count, UTC start/end, timezone/display semantics, and exact query semantics.
- Tests cover boundary timestamps, pagination/count correctness, timezone presentation, and API/query failures; failures are visible and fail closed.
- The measurement can be rerun by another session without relying on `/tmp` or session history.
- A checked-in policy requires duplicate and root-cause grouping before filing non-blocking manifestations.
- The policy defines a measurable positive-net threshold and an explicit slow/stop/group response.
- Blocker, security, and data-correctness findings remain immediate-file exceptions.
- The rolling seven-day target is negative net growth, and before/after observations are recorded.
- The implementation does not silently close, suppress, or relabel valid issues merely to improve the metric.

## Non-goals

- Do not count only current open issues; inflow and closure must both be measured.
- Do not use intake throttling as a substitute for delivery improvements in sibling issues.
- Do not weaken mandatory defect reporting for high-risk findings.

## Duplicate and boundary audit

This is cause B from #2512. It does not own delivery-PR consolidation (#2514), wait overlap (#2516), evidence ownership (#2517), transactional loop runs (#2504), or verification receipts (#2518).

Parent initiative: #2512

## Problem

Remote CI and review waits serialize the queue even though current policy already permits read-only exploration. The allowed seam is informal, so useful preflight is not consistently captured or distinguished from forbidden concurrent implementation.

## Recommended priority and cause

**P1.** Make read-only preflight a named, reusable workflow while retaining exactly one mutable delivery unit. This improves utilization but is secondary to the P0 lifecycle and intake causes.

## Expected behavior

While one PR is waiting on CI/review, a disjoint next issue may receive read-only dependency, blocker, source-location, duplicate, premise, lane, and owner analysis. No branch, Task conversion, implementation edit, or second mutable delivery unit is created for that next issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- The workflow defines exactly which operations and artifacts are read-only preflight and which cross into mutation.
- A reusable preflight output records subject issue, source/base identity, timestamp, evidence, assumptions, and invalidation conditions.
- The active PR remains the only mutable implementation unit.
- No second implementation branch is opened and no files for the preflight issue are edited.
- A mechanical guard or test rejects representative forbidden mutations while allowing the listed read-only checks.
- Stale preflight is revalidated when its source/base identity or relevant issue state changes.
- A following session can consume the preflight without treating it as conversion, PLAN approval, or implementation authorization.
- Before/after idle wait utilization is measured on at least one representative delivery.

## Non-goals

- Do not introduce parallel implementation branches.
- Do not let preflight reserve priority or bypass blocker/dependency rechecks.
- Do not duplicate conversion/PLAN consolidation from #2514.

## Duplicate and boundary audit

This is cause C from #2512. Its boundary is the reusable read-only handoff; workflow gate consolidation is #2514 and verification-stage parallelism is #2518.

## Problem

Approach, architecture, affected files, tests, scenario disposition, and verdict are repeatedly copied across Task, spec, PR, and gate/loop ledgers. Multiple editable copies add authoring/review time and can contradict one another without creating independent evidence.

## Recommended priority and cause

**P1.** Assign one canonical owner per fact and make other artifacts reference that owner. Preserve machine results and historical audit trails rather than deleting evidence.

## Canonical ownership target

- Task: problem, scope, issue linkage, urgency, lifecycle status
- Spec: accepted design, alternatives, affected files, completion criteria, test plan
- PR: links plus concise diff and verification summary
- Gate/loop ledger: machine result, subject identity, timestamps, and terminal status only

- Each repeated fact category has one documented owner and reference format.
- Non-owner templates and generators link or project from the owner instead of requiring independently edited prose.
- Mechanical checks detect missing owner references and stale or contradictory projections where feasible.
- Machine-generated verdicts and subject identities remain immutable/auditable.
- Historical records are preserved through prospective migration or explicit containment; no evidence is rewritten or fabricated.
- A representative work unit demonstrates materially less duplicated prose with no lost acceptance criterion, decision, or verdict.
- Readers can resolve every reference locally or through a stable repository/GitHub link; `/tmp` and session-only context are not dependencies.
- Failure to resolve a required owner is visible and cannot quietly pass a completion gate.

## Non-goals

- Do not collapse independent review into author-owned evidence.
- Do not replace machine receipts with prose links.
- Do not redesign PR lifecycle ordering (#2514) or receipt identity (#2518) here.

Parent initiative: #2512

## Problem

Targeted TDD, source-changing commit verification, post-implementation verification, pre-push checks, and remote CI can recompute overlapping evidence for an unchanged final tree. Existing receipt seams do not consistently prove every relevant input identity, and independent verification stages are not always scheduled as a dependency graph.

## Recommended priority and cause

**P2.** Define safe final-tree receipt identity/invalidation first, then parallelize only genuinely independent gates. This is lower priority because unsafe reuse can create false greens and the P0 causes dominate throughput.

## Expected behavior

Targeted tests run during RED/GREEN. A CI-equivalent final verification runs on the clean final HEAD, produces an identity-bound receipt, and may be reused only when every relevant input is identical. Independent stages execute in parallel where their declared dependencies permit.

## Acceptance criteria

- The receipt schema identifies commit/tree plus relevant source, configuration, dependency/lockfile, toolchain, environment contract, and gate-definition inputs.
- Any relevant input change invalidates reuse with a visible reason.
- Partial, failed, stale, dirty-tree, or differently scoped receipts cannot produce a green result.
- Pre-push and other consumers report whether a receipt was reused and the exact identity decision.
- The owner of each verification stage and its dependency edges are explicit; only independent stages run concurrently.
- Failures remain visible and fail closed; parallel execution does not hide or overwrite a failing result.
- Tests cover valid reuse and invalidation for source, config, dependency, toolchain, and gate-definition changes.
- Before/after wall time, duplicated-stage count, and cache/reuse hit rate are measured on a representative final HEAD.

## Non-goals

- Do not skip final clean-HEAD verification.
- Do not infer identity from a similar diff or branch name.
- Do not weaken remote CI or independent review merely because a local receipt exists.
- Do not own general evidence prose deduplication; that is #2517.

## Duplicate and boundary audit

This is cause F from #2512. #2514 owns PR lifecycle count, #2516 owns next-issue read-only preflight, and #2517 owns artifact fact ownership.

before.body:
Parent initiative: #1985

## Problem

`agent-cli` has no typed `mcpServers` setting, no canonical resolver, and no MCP management command. `BundlePluginLoader` can read a plugin `.mcp.json`, but exposes it as `mcpConfig?: unknown` and no production consumer resolves or activates it. Local, project, user, and plugin definitions therefore have no single source of truth.

## Recommended priority and cause

**P0 — configuration/control-plane foundation.** Product reachability cannot be implemented safely until every server definition is parsed, resolved, identified by provenance, and managed through one typed owner.

## Scope and ownership

- Define a typed, provider-neutral MCP server configuration contract at the lowest reusable boundary.
- Reuse the repository's existing layered settings stores and plugin loader as source adapters; do not create a parallel settings system.
- Resolve local, project, user, and plugin-provided entries with documented whole-entry precedence.
- Own enable/disable state and the owner APIs used by `agent-command` for add/import/list/get/remove/status operations.
- Keep activation authorization separate in the project/plugin trust child; resolution must not execute or connect.

## Acceptance criteria

- Local, project, and user scopes plus typed plugin-provided definitions resolve through one canonical API.
- Duplicate server names use an explicitly documented whole-entry winner; fields from different scopes are never silently merged.
- `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` expansion is supported only in declared fields. A missing variable without a default produces a visible warning and preserves the literal reference, matching the currently documented reference behavior unless the required AAR records a reasoned adaptation.
- Foreign-client `mcpServers` JSON can be imported through strict boundary validation with actionable diagnostics.
- Plugin `.mcp.json` is decoded into the same typed contract; `unknown` passthrough cannot reach execution.
- A server can be disabled and re-enabled without deleting its definition.
- `agent-command` exposes typed add/import/list/get/remove/status effects; `agent-cli` only composes and renders them.
- Secrets and expanded credential values are redacted from diagnostics and status output.
- Precedence, expansion, malformed input, duplicate names, plugin ingestion, and enable/disable behavior have deterministic tests.
- Listing or parsing configuration never starts a process or network connection.

## Parent checklist ownership

Owns scopes, whole-entry precedence, environment expansion, missing-variable behavior, JSON import, typed plugin servers, and disable-without-removal. Project/plugin activation approval is intentionally owned by a separate child.

## Non-goals and related issues

- Does not authorize project/plugin execution; see the activation-trust child.
- Does not implement HTTP/stdio transports or connection lifecycle.
- Does not create an MCP-specific settings stack beside the existing framework settings owners.
- #1986 is the opposite MCP-server direction; #2186 owns stale Task lifecycle.

## Moving reference

Re-read and record adopted/adapted/rejected decisions from the current [Claude Code MCP reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) before Task approval; this issue is a cause boundary, not a copy order.

Parent initiative: #1985

## Problem

A project or plugin MCP definition can ultimately start a local process or connect to a remote authority. Parsing and precedence do not answer whether a cloned repository or installed plugin is trusted to activate that definition. Treating source presence as execution approval would turn checked-in configuration into an implicit code-execution grant.

## Recommended priority and cause

**P0 — independent activation-security boundary.** Unsafe project/plugin activation would make the P0 client foundation unacceptable even if configuration parsing were correct.

## Scope and ownership

- Reuse the framework's workspace-authority/trusted-project seams.
- Preserve source provenance from configuration resolution through activation admission.
- Define explicit approve/reject/revoke flows for project- and plugin-provided servers.
- `agent-command` owns typed approval effects; `agent-cli` renders generic confirmation/status UI.
- Fail closed in an untrusted workspace and never let repository-tracked settings approve themselves.

## Acceptance criteria

- Project/plugin server definitions remain visible as pending or rejected without connecting or spawning.
- An untrusted workspace cannot activate its own checked-in approval, server command, helper command, or remote endpoint.
- Approval identifies the exact server definition, source provenance, and security-relevant identity; material definition changes invalidate prior approval.
- User/managed authority and local untracked approval sources have explicit precedence and cannot be weakened by project content.
- Approve, reject, revoke, and status flows are observable and auditable without exposing secrets.
- Activation admission is a reusable port; transports cannot bypass it by calling lower clients directly.
- Tests cover cloned/untrusted workspaces, self-approval attempts, plugin provenance, changed definitions, rejection, revocation, and trusted activation.
- Configuration inspection and health/status commands do not accidentally activate a pending server.

## Parent checklist ownership

Owns the trust decision required when project/plugin-provided configuration becomes executable. It is separated from configuration resolution because it has a different threat model and terminal decision.

## Non-goals and related issues

- Does not define scope parsing or precedence; the configuration/control-plane child supplies typed definitions and provenance.
- Does not implement stdio subprocess restrictions, OAuth, or `headersHelper`; those remain separate defense layers.
- Does not allow the CLI presentation package to own trust policy.

## Moving reference

Revalidate project-server approval and workspace-trust behavior in the current [Claude Code MCP reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp), then record Robota's adopted/adapted/rejected decision.
